subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should SMS webhook ingress accept up to 300 failed requests per minute per account route and resolved client, with over-budget rejection deferred until the request is known invalid, to preserve a separate 30/min valid-callback capacity?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish correctness, but the amount of unauthenticated parsing and HMAC-validation work tolerated in exchange for avoiding callback starvation is a product security and availability policy choice.

options.title: Accept the two-stage boundary
options.body: Merge the current 300/min failed-request budget and independent 30/min dispatch cap as the intended SMS webhook policy.

options.title: Retune before merge
options.body: Choose a lower failed-request threshold while preserving the separate valid-callback quota and current key scope.

options.title: Keep the strict pre-auth gate
options.body: Decline this tradeoff and retain the existing 30/min pre-validation behavior, accepting that same-key invalid traffic can block valid callbacks.

recommendation.title: Accept the two-stage boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the current 300/min failed-request budget and independent 30/min dispatch cap as the intended SMS webhook policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the SMS webhook and original limiter, so they are the strongest available owner for this boundary decision.
